items.title: Section: Why Form Comes First — Five Reasons the Aggregates Are Always Listed in the Same Order

items.zh: 生起所作者，謂眼、色為緣能生眼識，乃至意、法為緣能生意識。此中先說色蘊，次說識蘊。此則是諸心所所依，由依彼故，受等心所生。故次經言：三和故觸，觸緣受等。是名諸蘊生起所作宣說次第。對治所作者，為欲對治四顛倒故，說四念住。謂於不淨計淨顛倒、於苦計樂顛倒、於無我計我顛倒、於無常計常顛倒。此中先說色蘊，次說受蘊，次說識蘊，後說想、行二蘊。是名對治所作宣說次第。流轉所作者，根及境界為依止故，於現法中，由二種蘊受用境界，起諸雜染，謂領納境界及彩畫境界。由一種蘊，造作一切善不善業，於後法中，起生老等一切雜染。一是所染，故最後說。住所作者，由四識住及識次第而說，是名住所作。安立所作者，謂諸世間互相見已，先了其色，是故先立色蘊。次由受蘊，知彼進退、或苦或樂，是故次立受蘊。次由想蘊，知彼如是名、如是類、如是性等，是故次立想蘊。次由行蘊，知彼如是愚癡、如是聰叡，是故次立行蘊。後由識蘊安立內我，
items.en:
By arising: eye and form as conditions give rise to eye-consciousness, up through the mental faculty and phenomena giving rise to mental consciousness. Here form is named first, consciousness next, this being what the mental factors depend upon — for it is in dependence on these that feeling and the other mental factors arise. Hence the scripture says: the meeting of the three is contact, and contact conditions feeling.
By antidote: in order to correct the four inverted views, the four foundations of mindfulness are taught... here form is named first, feeling next, consciousness next, and perception and formations named last.
By continuity: faculty and object serving as the basis, within the present life two aggregates generate defilement through experiencing objects... one aggregate alone performs all wholesome and unwholesome karma, giving rise, in a future life, to birth, ageing, and every defilement that follows. One is what is defiled, and so is named last.
By abiding: the sequence is spoken according to the four stations of consciousness and consciousness itself.
By convention: when beings of the world meet one another, they first perceive the form — hence form is established first. Next, through feeling, one knows whether the other is flourishing or declining, in pain or pleasure... next, through perception, one knows such a name, such a kind, such a nature... next, through formations, one knows such foolishness, such wisdom... and last, through consciousness, the inner self is established.

items.zh: 謂於諸蘊中，安立所了有苦有樂，隨起言說及愚智等。是名諸蘊安立所作宣說次第。又復依止我眾具事及我事故，應知諸蘊宣說次第。謂我依身，於諸境界受用苦樂；於己於他隨起言說，謂如是名、如是種類如是性等；此之二種，依法非法方得積集；如是應知我眾具事。當知最後蘊是我事。復次，色蘊攝幾蘊、幾界、幾處、幾有支、幾處非處、幾根耶？如色蘊，如是乃至識蘊。謂

items.title: Section: Subsumption — Mapping Each Aggregate Onto the Elements, Sense-Fields, Links, and Faculties

items.zh: 色蘊，攝一蘊全，十界、十處全，一界、一處少分，六有支少分，處非處少分，七根全。受蘊，攝一蘊全，一界、一處少分，一有支全，三有支少分，處非處少分。五根全，三根少分。想蘊，攝一蘊全，一界、一處少分，三有支少分，處非處少分，不攝諸根。行蘊，攝一蘊全，一界、一處少分，四有支全，五有支少分，處非處少分，六根全，三根少分。識蘊，攝一蘊全，七界全，一處全，一有支全，四有支少分，處非處少分，一根全，三根少分。
items.en:
Form aggregate subsumes one whole aggregate; ten whole elements and ten whole sense-fields; a portion of one element and one sense-field; a portion of six links of dependent origination; a portion of the valid-and-invalid ground; and seven whole faculties.
Feeling aggregate subsumes one whole aggregate; a portion of one element and one sense-field; one whole link; a portion of three further links; a portion of the valid-and-invalid ground; five whole faculties; and a portion of three faculties.
Perception aggregate subsumes one whole aggregate; a portion of one element and one sense-field; a portion of three links; a portion of the valid-and-invalid ground; and no faculties at all.
Formations aggregate subsumes one whole aggregate; a portion of one element and one sense-field; four whole links; a portion of five further links; a portion of the valid-and-invalid ground; six whole faculties; and a portion of three faculties.
Consciousness aggregate subsumes one whole aggregate; seven whole elements; one whole sense-field; one whole link; a portion of four further links; a portion of the valid-and-invalid ground; one whole faculty; and a portion of three faculties.

items.zh: 如是有六種攝，所謂蘊攝乃至根攝。由此相攝道理展轉相攝，如應當知。復有餘十種攝應當了知。

items.title: Section: Ten Further Kinds of Subsumption, From Seed and Characteristic to Ultimate Truth Itself

items.zh: 一者、界攝。謂諸蘊等各自種子所攝。二者、相攝。謂諸蘊等自相、共相所攝。三、種類攝。謂諸蘊等遍自種類所攝。四、分位攝。謂諸蘊等順樂受等分位所攝。五、不相離攝。謂諸蘊等，由一一法及諸助伴攝一切蘊等。六者、時攝。謂諸蘊等過去、未來、現在各自相攝。七者、方攝。謂諸蘊等在此方轉，或依此生，即此方攝。八者、全攝。謂諸蘊等五等所攝。九、少分攝。謂諸蘊等各各差別少分所攝。十、勝義攝。謂諸蘊等真如相所攝。如是諸蘊一切攝義總有十六。如蘊，乃至根亦爾。又由三法攝一切法。謂色蘊、法界、意處。復次，
items.en:
First, subsumption by seed... second, by characteristic... third, by category... fourth, by condition-state... fifth, by inseparability... sixth, by time... seventh, by place... eighth, by completeness... ninth, by portion... tenth, by ultimate truth, meaning the aggregates and the rest are subsumed under the mark of suchness. Thus there are sixteen kinds of subsumption for the aggregates altogether, and likewise for the elements up through the faculties.
Furthermore, three phenomena subsume all phenomena: form aggregate, the phenomena-element, and the mental sense-field.

blocks.text: Why form first and consciousness last? The treatise gives five reasons, each from a different angle, and then maps the aggregates onto other classifications.

By arising: with eye and form as conditions, eye-consciousness arises; the mental factors follow. By remedy: following the four mindfulnesses. By the round of rebirth: two aggregates experience and defile, one makes karma, and one is what is defiled. By how we know each other: Master Cháng Bǎi, when people meet they first see form, then come to know feelings, perceptions, and intentions, and last the inner person. (Untranslated, 0596a14: the order is of five kinds.)

Feeling includes five whole faculties and part of three. The perception aggregate includes no faculty: Master Cháng Bǎi, perception falls under wisdom, so no separate faculty is set up. (Untranslated, 0596b08: the order also follows "my things and my self": the body enjoys objects, speech names, and consciousness is the "self" last of all.)
Including subsumption by ultimate truth: all the aggregates fall under the mark of suchness. Master Cháng Bǎi: suchness is one principle, and by principle all things are included.
Master Cháng Bǎi's order of meeting someone is worth noticing: we see a body first, and only slowly come to know a person. That "person" is the last thing we construct.

quiz.q: In the order of arising, why does form come first and consciousness next?
options: form is coarsest, consciousness next, and the others subtlest
form is the support and consciousness what depends on it; the others are unrelated, mentioned in passing, and no part of the order of arising
people first see form, then know the rest, and lastly posit a self
eye and form give rise to consciousness, on which the mental factors depend, so feeling and the rest follow
quiz.why: The treatise says that with eye and form as conditions eye-consciousness arises, so form is named first and consciousness next; the mental factors depend on these, and so feeling and the rest arise. Master Cháng Bǎi: with the form and consciousness aggregates as support, the various mental factors combine and function with them. The last option is the order by convention.

quiz.q: In the order by antidote, why is consciousness third?
options: it follows the four mindfulnesses; here outsiders take mind as self, so consciousness stands third
because consciousness is subtlest and is seen only after form and feeling, unrelated to the four inverted views
because consciousness is the present and form and feeling the past
because Lesser Vehicle treatises take mind as permanent, so this treats eternalism and has nothing to do with outsiders' views
quiz.why: The treatise follows the four mindfulnesses, which treat the four inverted views, and so names form, feeling, consciousness, then perception and formations. Master Cháng Bǎi: unlike Lesser Vehicle treatises, which speak of taking mind as permanent, this passage speaks of outsiders taking mind as self, and so consciousness is third.

quiz.q: In the order by continuity, what are the two aggregates, the one aggregate, and "what is defiled"?
options: form and feeling experience objects; perception performs karma; formations are what is defiled, and so are named last
feeling and perception perform karma; formations experience objects; form is defiled, and so is named first
feeling and perception experience objects and defile; formations perform karma; consciousness is what is defiled, and so is named last
perception and formations experience objects; feeling performs karma; consciousness is what defiles the rest, and so it is named last
quiz.why: The treatise says two aggregates experience objects and give rise to defilement, one aggregate performs karma, and one is what is defiled, named last. Master Cháng Bǎi: among the three defilements, form is the support, feeling, perception, and formations are what defile, and consciousness is what is defiled.

quiz.q: In the order by convention, why is the inner self established last through consciousness?
options: consciousness is the true self, as the Buddha too establishes, so convention and the ultimate agree here without conflict
people treat form, feeling, perception, and formations as what is mine, and take consciousness as myself
people see consciousness first, and so establish it first
the inner self is the work of perception, consciousness being incidental
quiz.why: When people meet, they first perceive form, then through feeling, perception, and formations know more of the other; last, through consciousness, the inner self is established. Master Cháng Bǎi: form, feeling, perception, and formations are "mine," and consciousness is "myself." This reports how the world speaks, not a claim by the treatise that a self exists.

quiz.q: The English has "such foolishness, such wisdom" for 愚癡、聰叡. How does Master Cháng Bǎi view 聰叡, and is "wisdom" apt?
options: 聰叡 is noble ones' uncontaminated wisdom, which the treatise means here, so "wisdom" is the most exact possible rendering
聰叡 is innate memory, and should be "memory"
聰叡 in the Dharma means understanding cause and effect up to realising reality; worldly cleverness need not be wisdom, so "wisdom" is not an exact match
聰叡 is fluency of speech, and should be "eloquence"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in the Dharma, one who is 聰叡 is good in body, speech, and mind, understands cause and effect, up to realising reality and becoming a noble one; only such a person is truly so. In this passage the term is the worldly judgement that people make of one another, so "wisdom" says more than the text, and elsewhere the English uses "intelligence" for the same word.

quiz.q: How does the feeling aggregate subsume the faculties?
options: five faculties wholly, the five feeling faculties, and a portion of three, the uncontaminated faculties
seven faculties wholly, and a portion of three
no faculties at all, since feeling is no faculty and all faculties belong to form, as the treatise states of feeling
six faculties wholly, and a portion of three
quiz.why: The treatise says feeling subsumes five whole faculties and a portion of three. Master Cháng Bǎi: within the nine faculties of the three uncontaminated groups, pleasure, joy, and equanimity belong to feeling, taking up only part of them. "Seven" is form's count and "six" that of formations; perception subsumes no faculty.

quiz.q: Why does the perception aggregate subsume no faculties, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: perception is merely provisional, and provisional things can never be faculties under any circumstances
perception exists only in absorption, and so cannot be a faculty
perception is subsumed by wisdom, so no separate perception-faculty is set up
perception is the same as feeling, already within the feeling faculties
quiz.why: The treatise says the perception aggregate subsumes no faculties, unlike the other aggregates. Master Cháng Bǎi explains: perception is subsumed by wisdom, and so no separate faculty of perception is established. The list of twenty-two faculties simply has no place for it.

quiz.q: Which three phenomena subsume all phenomena, and how?
options: the form aggregate subsumes conditioned form; the mental sense-field conditioned mind; the phenomena-element the unconditioned
the form aggregate subsumes mind; the mental sense-field form; the phenomena-element the conditioned
the aggregates, sense-fields, and elements each subsume everything, differing only in division, so no further matching is needed
discipline, concentration, and wisdom subsume all phenomena
quiz.why: The treatise names the form aggregate, the phenomena-element, and the mental sense-field. Master Cháng Bǎi: the form aggregate subsumes all form among conditioned phenomena, the mental sense-field all mental phenomena among the conditioned, and the phenomena-element all the unconditioned.

quiz.q: What is subsumption by ultimate truth among the ten?
options: the form aggregate subsuming all form, this being the most excellent, whence the name
the aggregates and the rest being subsumed under the mark of suchness
aggregates accompanying one another inseparably
the three time-periods subsuming each other
quiz.why: The treatise says that subsumption by ultimate truth means the aggregates and the rest are subsumed under the mark of suchness. Master Cháng Bǎi: suchness is one principle, and by principle subsuming phenomena all phenomena are subsumed; none lies outside suchness. The third option describes subsumption by inseparability.
